knownIssues.title: Accelerated battery capacity loss without active thermal management
knownIssues.description: No liquid battery cooling means faster capacity loss with frequent DC fast charging or hot climates, usually noticeable from ~60,000-80,000 km; range drops, safety unaffected.

fixes.summary: Confirm degradation with a battery health check
fixes.steps: 1) Confirm lower range/capacity vs original rating; read SOH if possible. 2) Tools: OBD-II adapter, LeafSpy or equivalent. 3) Log SOH over a few charge cycles. 4) Compare against expected degradation for year/mileage. 5) Escalate only if SOH is abnormally low for mileage.

fixes.summary: Prefer AC charging and moderate charge limits to slow further degradation
fixes.steps: 1) Confirm frequent DC fast charging or routine 100% charge. 2) Tools: none - usage change. 3) Prefer AC charging and ~80% daily limit when available. 4) Check SOH decline slows over following months. 5) No workshop needed - preventive habit.

fixes.summary: Replace or recondition the traction battery pack
fixes.steps: 1) Confirm severe SOH/range loss before replacement. 2) Tools: HV pack, specialist tooling and PPE. 3) Certified EV tech removes, fits and re-commissions pack. 4) Verify SOH and a full charge/range test. 5) Always certified EV workshop - never DIY HV pack work.

knownIssues.title: Onboard charger (OBC) intermittent AC charging faults
knownIssues.description: Intermittent OBC faults stop, slow or block AC charging while DC fast charging still works; limits daily use, not driving safety.

fixes.summary: Diagnose the onboard charger with a dealer scan tool
fixes.steps: 1) Confirm fault persists with another cable/wallbox. 2) Tools: dealer-level EV diagnostic scanner. 3) Tech reads HV codes to isolate OBC vs port/cable. 4) Clear codes and complete a full AC charge. 5) Workshop with EV tooling, not generic OBD-II.

fixes.summary: Replace a faulty onboard charger unit
fixes.steps: 1) Confirm OBC is the fault, not cable/port. 2) Tools: replacement OBC, HV isolation equipment. 3) Certified EV tech isolates HV, replaces OBC, re-commissions. 4) Verify full AC charge at slow and higher rates. 5) Always certified EV workshop.

knownIssues.title: 12V auxiliary battery drain and failure
knownIssues.description: Failed or drained 12V auxiliary battery prevents the car from waking the HV system even with a charged traction battery, often after long sits.

fixes.summary: Test and replace the 12V auxiliary battery
fixes.steps: 1) Confirm no power-on/charge despite healthy HV pack; 12V tests low. 2) Tools: multimeter/tester, correct-spec 12V battery. 3) Test and replace if failed; check polarity and terminals. 4) Confirm vehicle powers on and charges. 5) DIY for basic 12V swap; escalate if DC-DC converter suspected.
